name: session
description: Resume an interrupted turn, audit or hand off a session, arm a rate-limit safety net, defer a command, and spawn or tear down isolated git worktrees.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the session skills.

The authoritative mapping is not in this repo. It lives in the sibling repo `dEitY719/harness-skills` at `references/kimi-tools.md` (https://github.com/dEitY719/harness-skills/blob/main/references/kimi-tools.md) and is the single source of truth for every repo in the `dEitY719/*-skills` family; do not copy it here. Summary:

- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Search contents with `Grep`; match paths with `Glob`. The `lib/*.sh` helpers under `skills/close/` are plain bash - run them with `Bash` and pass their `BLOCKED:` / `NOTE:` / `WARN:` lines through verbatim; do not reimplement them.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or `"explore"` (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`. `session:restart` delegates every broad search or full-tree scan this way, on purpose: the premise is that the last turn died, so the main context must stay lean.
- "Ask the user" -> `AskUserQuestion`. `session:worktree-teardown` deletes a worktree and a branch; when its pre-flight finds uncommitted changes or unpushed commits it must stop and let the user decide, never pass `--force` on its own.
- Kimi Code has no `Skill` tool. Where `session:handoff` says `Skill(gh-issue:create)`, either read that skill's `SKILL.md` from the `gh-*` plugin and follow it inline, or open the tracking issue directly with `gh issue create`. The handoff contract is just an issue number.
- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool. It writes; it does not replay a finished session's list. Claude Code's `TaskList` / `TaskUpdate` have no Kimi equivalent, so the three skills that read the session TodoList degrade: `session:restart` picks its resume target from the last completed tool result in the conversation instead of from `in_progress`, `session:close` reports C-2 as "TodoList unavailable on this harness" rather than skipping it silently, and `session:handoff` pulls remaining work from the conversation.
- `CronCreate` / `CronDelete` have no Kimi equivalent at all. `session:rate-limit-guard`, `session:resume-after-limit`, and `session:schedule` cannot run here. Say so and stop - do not emulate a cron with a sleep, a background process, or a promise to act later.

Safety contracts. These are part of the skills, not advice:

- `session:close` is strictly read-only. It creates, edits, and deletes nothing, changes no git state, and sends nothing to a remote. It prints remediation commands; the user decides whether to run them. It never invokes `/exit` on the user's behalf.
- `session:handoff` writes exactly two artifacts: one issue comment and one memory file. No commits, no pushes, no code edits, no issue state changes. Only merged PRs and tests that ran green in this session may be listed as done - unverified work is labeled as such, and the resume sentence must map to the real tracking issue.
- `session:worktree-teardown` is the destructive one. Run it from the main repo, never from inside the worktree being removed. Block on uncommitted changes or unpushed commits; `--force` is the user's explicit override, not yours. Sync main before deleting the branch so `git branch -d` can verify merge status.
- `session:worktree-spawn` refuses to run from inside an existing worktree, and in a git-crypt repo it uses explicit `git add <path>` - never `-A` or `.` - because auto-unlocked files can show as modified from a raw-byte versus textconv mismatch.
- `session:restart` is user-triggered recovery, never a building block: no other skill may invoke it. It never re-runs a process skill whose output is already in the conversation, and it never batches tool calls - the premise is that the last batch died mid-way.

interface.shortDescription: Resume, close, hand off, schedule, and isolate a coding session
interface.longDescription: Session bundles the eight session-lifecycle skills: restart, close, handoff, rate-limit-guard, resume-after-limit, schedule, worktree-spawn, and worktree-teardown. The three cron-driven ones are Claude Code only.
